newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan premium widens ahead of year-end.
newsitem.headline: Japan premium widens ahead of year-end.

text.p: The Japan premium -- the extra cost Japanese banks are charged when raising funds in the Euro interbank market -- rose further on Tuesday due to foreign banks' reluctance to lend money ahead of the end-year book closing, money traders said.
Major Japanese city banks were paying a premium of about 31 to 41 basis points (BPS) over the prevailing one-month Eurodollar deposit rate of 5.59375 percent.
This compared with a premium of about 25 BPS last week.

"Foreign banks are generally reluctant to lend money before they close their books for the fiscal year-end in December. This is forcing Japanese banks to raise their bids to procure funds," said a money trader, adding that the premium may widen further before the end of this year.

The premium for major Japanese city banks was close to zero until debt-laden Hanwa Bank Ltd, a regional bank in western Japan, was ordered to halt operations by regulators in late November, traders said.
Some banks with funding difficulties in the Euro interbank market also tapped the forward dollar/yen market and converted yen into dollars to meet their liquidity needs, they said.
